3.text: The Nasik inscription was issued by Gautami Balasri during the reign of Vasishtiputra Pulomavi.
The Nasik inscription mentions the military achievements of Gautamiputra Satakarni.
Ushavadatta invested 2,000 Karshapanas in a weavers’ guild.
The interest rate on Ushavadatta’s investment was 12%.
Myakadoni is associated with Pulumavi IV.
Pulumavi IV was the last Satavahana king.
V. V. Sukthankar located the Satavahanas in Bellary.
Gulmika means a feudatory chief.
The Kodavali inscription is associated with Chanda Satakarni.
The Junnar inscription was issued by Aayama.
The Pithapuram inscription is associated with Prithvisvara of Velanadu.
The Pithapuram inscription mentions Kolleru Lake.
The Magallu inscription is associated with Danarnava.
The Magallu inscription contains the first mention of the Kakatiyas.
The Gurazala inscription was issued by Rudrapurushadatta of the Ikshvaku dynasty.
The Alluru inscription is associated with Ehavala Chamtamula.
The Alluru inscription records multiple gifts to different sections and institutions.
The Marturu inscription is associated with Pulakesin II.
The Marturu inscription refers to Mangalagiri as Mangalapura.
The Vipparla inscription was issued by Jayasimha Vallabha.
The Dharmasagar inscription is associated with the Kakatiyas.
Dharmasagar is also called Dharmasagaram.
The Dharmasagar inscription mentions the musical instrument Jalakaranda.
The Porumamilla inscription is associated with Prince Bhaskara Bhavadura.
The Porumamilla inscription contains 12 rules for tank construction.
The Kalamalla inscription was issued by Erikal Mutthuraju Dhananjaya Varma.
The Kalamalla inscription is the first inscription in Telugu.
The Bhattiprolu inscription is associated with Raja Kubhiraka.
The Bhattiprolu inscription mentions the Nigama-sabha of the Satavahanas.
Kubhiraka was the ruler mentioned in the Bhattiprolu inscription.
Kubhiraka belonged to the 3rd century BC.
The Erragudi inscription is associated with Ashoka.
The Erragudi inscription records Ashoka’s instruction to teachers to inculcate Dharma in students.
The Ganapatideva inscription was found at Motupalli.
The Anamakonda inscription is associated with Rudra Deva.
The Anamakonda inscription records the success stories of Rudra Deva.
The Draksharama inscription is associated with Rudradeva.
The Draksharama inscription narrates Rudra Deva as Vinaya Bhushan.
The Tripuranthakam inscription is associated with Ambadeva.
The Tripuranthakam inscription records the victorious achievements of Amba Deva.
The Musunuri Nayaka inscription is associated with Prolaya Nayaka.
Pratapa Rudra died by jumping into the Narmada.
The Anitalli inscription was issued by Kaluva Anitalli.
Prolaya Vema Reddy served in Kapaya Nayaka’s Cheru court.
The Manyamapura inscription is associated with Anapota Reddy.
Anapota Reddy shifted the capital from Addanki to Kondaveedu.
The Mani Kesavara inscription is associated with Prolaya Vema Reddy.
Prolaya Vema Reddy ruled until 1353.
The Mutnuri inscription is associated with Prolaya Vema Reddy.
The Mutnuri inscription records the completion of the steps to Pathala Ganga at Srisailam in 1346.
The Santhana Sagaram inscription is associated with Srinatha, the author.
Surambika was the queen of Pedakomati Vema.
Surambika was associated with the tank mentioned in the Santhana Sagaram inscription.
The Kondamudi record is a copper edict.
The Kondamudi copper edict was issued by Jayavarma of the Brihatpalayana dynasty.
The Kondamudi copper edict is the only inscription about the Brihatpalayanas.
The Kondamudi copper edict was issued in the 10th year of Jayavarma’s reign.
The Nagarjunakonda inscription is associated with the Ikshvaku dynasty.
The Brihatpalayanas were feudatories of the Ikshvakus.
The Pedavegi inscription was issued by Nandi Varma II of the Salankayana dynasty.
The Pedavegi inscription records a grant of land to Vishnu.
The Pedavegi inscription is the first to mention Vishnu temples in Andhra.
The Kolleru inscription was issued by Nandi Varma II.
The Eluru inscription is associated with Devavarma.
The Eluru inscription mentions Munyada, meaning a political employee.
The Kazipet inscription is associated with Betha Raju II and Durgaraja.
Durga Nripathi ascended the throne.
The Chejerla inscription is associated with Kandararaju.
The Chejerla inscription records wars between the Ikshvakus and the Anandagotrikas.
The Manchikallu inscription is associated with Simhavarma.
The Manchikallu inscription was found near Vijayapuri.
The Manchikallu inscription is similar to the Nagarjunakonda inscription.
Upasika Bodhisri is associated with evidence of Buddhism patronage under the Ikshvakus.
The Allahabad Pillar inscription was issued by Samudragupta.
The Allahabad Pillar inscription mentions Hastivarma of the Salankayana dynasty.

1.text: Andhra was the first linguistic state of India.
Andhra State was formed in April 1953 after separation from Madras State.
Tanguturi Prakasam was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953.
Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in 1956.
Chandulal Madhavlal Trivedi was the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956.
Nallapati Venkatramaiah was the first Speaker of Andhra State in 1953.
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
Dr. N. Sanjeeva Reddy was the first Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra State.
K. V. Rangareddy was the first Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the last Chief Minister of Andhra State.
The Andhra Pradesh Legislature became bicameral for the first time in 1958.
The first Andhra Mahasabha or Andhra Conference was held on 26 May 1913 at Bapatla.
B. N. Sharma presided over the first Andhra Mahasabha or Andhra Conference.
The first Andhra Mahasabha was the first Telugu session.
The first Andhra Mahasabha demanded a separate university.
The first Rayalaseema Mahasabha is associated with 28 January 1934/1936 and Madras.
Nyapati Subba Rao was the first President of the Andhra Congress Circle.
Govinda Rao Nanal was the first President of the Hyderabad State Congress.
M. Annapurnayya was the first Secretary of the Socialist Party’s Andhra unit.
N. G. Ranga was the first President of the Andhra Socialist Party.
P. Anandacharyulu was the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress.
P. Anandacharyulu became the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress in 1891 at Nagpur.
Mulla Abdul Qayyum was the first Muslim leader from Hyderabad to join the Indian National Congress.
B. Ramakrishna Rao was the first elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State.
The Kakinada Riot Case was the first criminal case in the Vandemataram Movement.
Chintapalli was the first police station attacked by Alluri Sitarama Raju.
Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi was the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha.
Nyapati Subba Rao was the first lawyer in Andhra to boycott British courts.
The Forest Satyagraha first started in Palnadu, Guntur.
The first widow remarriage in Andhra took place on 11 December 1881.
Veeresalingam conducted the first widow remarriage in Andhra at Rajahmundry.
Rajasekhara Charitram was the first novel in Telugu.
Veeresalingam wrote Rajasekhara Charitram.
Satya Doota was the first Telugu journal.
Satya Doota was published at Bellary.
Andhra Prakasika was the first political journal in Andhra.
The Bible was the first book printed in Telugu.
Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was the first Telugu library in Hyderabad.
Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was established in 1901.
Komarraju Lakshmana Rao was associated with Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam.
C. P. Brown compiled the first English–Telugu dictionary.
The first Kisan School was established at Nidubrolu.
N. G. Ranga was associated with the first Kisan School at Nidubrolu.
The first World Telugu Conference was held in 1975.
Viswanatha Satyanarayana was the first Telugu recipient of the Jnanpith Award.
H. M. Reddy was the first Telugu cinema director.
The Satavahanas were the first historical ruling dynasty of the Deccan.
Harihara-I was the first ruler of Vijayanagara.
Devaraya-I was the first Vijayanagara monarch to enlist Muslims in the army.
The Kalamalla inscription was the first inscription in Telugu.
The Magallu inscription mentioned the Kakatiyas for the first time.
The first Muslim invasion of Warangal took place in 1303.
Kulottunga-I was the first Chalukya-Chola emperor.
Nannaya was the first poet to translate the Mahabharata into Telugu.
Alauddin Khilji led the first sultanate invasion of the Kakatiyas.
The first Dutch factory in Andhra was established at Masulipatnam, also known as Machilipatnam.
The English established their first factory at Machilipatnam.
The English factory at Machilipatnam was established in 1611.
Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah granted permission for the English factory at Machilipatnam.
Hyderabad was the first Indian state to sign the Subsidiary Alliance.
Ryotwari was first introduced in the Madras Presidency at Baramahals.
The first All-India Congress session held in Andhra took place at Vijayawada.
